subject: Request: executive clearance for most-favored status + limited exclusivity (NexaHealth EMEA)

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Proposal: EMEA deployment agreement — initial commercial and terms

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday. Attached is the draft SOW and a regional price matrix for the EMEA pilot we discussed. High level: 12-month committed term, 20% list discount off our standard hosted rates, and a recommended implementation timeline targeting production in Q1.

Two items I want to call out up front that came up in the meeting:
- Nexa asked for a Most‑Favored status (price-matching clause) across comparable enterprise customers in the EU.
- They also requested a short-term exclusivity carveout for Redwood in EMEA for certain payer/government segments for the first 3 months after go-live.

Both are outside our standard playbook—looping Hannah and Rishi for visibility and early guidance. From a commercial perspective this is a ~$1.1M ARR commitment if they sign for the 12-month term.

Next steps: Priya, if you can confirm the list of segments you'd expect in the exclusivity scope we can mark those in the SOW. I’ll be available to walk legal and ops through the ask if helpful.

Attachments: NexaHealth_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf (stubs), price_matrix_EMEA.xlsx (stubs)

Regards,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Nexa — procurement asks (MFN + short exclusivity) — request for exec clearance

Hannah — forwarding Priya's note. Deal context in short:
- ACV expected: ~$1.1M (12-month committed consumption, hosted API).
- Upside potential: regional rollouts across FR/DE/UK in next 12 months.
- Procurement is explicitly asking for MFN language + 3-month exclusivity for EMEA payer segment.

My proposed compromise for consideration:
- MFN: limited to list price parity on equivalent published offers (no retroactive benchmarking obligations), apply only to base hosted unit price (exclude ancillary professional services and add-ons).
- Exclusivity: narrow to two named payer sub-segments and limit to 90 days post-go-live; include an explicit carve-out for partners and existing government procurement frameworks.
- Financial floor: discount cannot exceed 30% of list; we hold ability to offer deeper promos to strategic reference customers with legal sign‑off.

Request: Can you provide executive clearance to accept the above compromise? If yes, legal will draft a short addendum and finance will confirm the discount floor. If no, please advise on limits we should push back on before returning to Priya.

Attaching: exec-clearance-draft.docx (stubs)

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:17:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexa — procurement asks (MFN + short exclusivity) — risk assessment

Marcus / Hannah — quick legal read:

MFN concerns:
- "Most‑Favored" is highly contextual — if written broadly it can require retroactive price adjustments and create a race-to-the-bottom for future deals.
- Suggest limiting MFN to: (a) published list pricing for equivalent SaaS/hosted offerings; (b) a narrow product scope (exclude add-ons, quantization/hosting tier upgrades); (c) a look‑forward only clause (no retroactive true‑up).

Exclusivity concerns:
- Exclusivity for the payer segment could block go‑to‑market partnerships and conflict with resale or marketplace agreements.
- Recommend: duration cap of 90 days, geographic cap (EMEA), segment-specific definition with examples, explicit carve-outs for existing marketplace/reseller agreements and emergency security exceptions.

Operational asks if we accept in principle:
1) Include an audit right limited to pricing comparisons and only on reasonable notice.
2) Define objective equivalence criteria (customer size, product configuration) to avoid broad benchmarking disputes.
3) Sunset the MFN after 12 months unless renewed by mutual written agreement.

If leadership is willing to clear with the above guardrails and the 30% discount floor (finance to confirm), legal can prepare the addendum and a short exec signoff memo for signature. Otherwise we should push back and offer the alternative: a 10% additional discount and an exclusivity-free reference arrangement.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexa — procurement asks (MFN + short exclusivity) — exec decision

Team — thanks for the clear framing. Executives have reviewed and I can grant conditional clearance to proceed with the customer under the following constraints (must be documented in the addendum):

1) MFN: Limited, forward‑looking price‑matching restricted to our published hosted unit price for equivalent configurations sold in the EU. No retroactive true‑ups; excludes professional services, premium support tiers, and any custom integrations. MFN to expire after 12 months from contract effective date unless explicitly renewed.

2) Exclusivity: Approved only for a 90‑day period post‑go-live, narrowly scoped to the two payer sub‑segments Marcus identified (list to be included in the SOW). Must include carve‑outs for (a) reseller/marketplace channel agreements pre‑existing at signature, and (b) security/emergency procurements.

3) Pricing floor: Discount cannot exceed 30% off list on the hosted unit price. Any deeper concession requires VP-level signoff and written rationale.

4) Audit & equivalence metrics: Legal to include an objective equivalence definition (customer size, ARR band, product module parity). Audits allowed only on 30 days' notice and limited to pricing documentation.

5) Reporting & sunset: Add automatic sunset of MFN at 12 months and require a quarterly revenue/usage review with Finance for the first year.

Laura — please prepare the addendum and an exec signoff memo consistent with the bullets above. Rishi — please confirm the finance floor (30% is acceptable) and flag any P&L headwinds. Marcus — revert to Priya with the proposed guardrails and the timeline for redlines (legal will aim to return within 48 hours once draft is ready).

I want clean, objective language — no open-ended benchmarking obligations. If Nexa pushes for retroactive true-ups or broader language, we walk.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
